source.title: Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models
source.authors: Luis Barroso-Luque; Muhammed Shuaibi; Xiang Fu; Brandon M. Wood; Misko Dzamba; Meng Gao; Ammar Rizvi; C. Zitnick; Zachary W. Ulissi

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a materials-model dataset-size learning curve, but does not test the language-model power laws or fit-dependence described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Supplementary Figure D.1 reports eSEN prediction-error curves as the OMat24 training subset grows. This is a related materials-model result, not a test of held-out language-model cross-entropy or of a power-law fit. The paper also cites scaling-law work; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a dataset-and-models paper for materials interatomic potentials. It cites Kaplan et al. only to motivate large datasets. Its one data-size learning curve (Fig. D.1) is not fitted or assessed as a power law, and the text reports a plateau rather than a scaling law. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the supplementary learning curve. The authors' main conclusion is broader. OMat24 (over 110M DFT calculations) trains MLIPs that set state-of-the-art Matbench Discovery results (eSEN F1 0.925, about 18 meV/atom energy-above-hull MAE). It also reduces or eliminates systematic softening across architectures. The dataset-size learning curve is a supplementary observation: errors drop with data and plateau near 100M samples.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies materials interatomic potentials and dataset-size learning curves, not the original language-model scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size changes the reported errors.

fits_no_version.finding: For eSEN trained on OMat24 subsamples (1e5 to 1e8 structures), energy and force MAE decrease with training-set size and plateau near 100M samples (Fig. D.1, no fit reported).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For materials MLIPs, test error falls with training-set size until a plateau near the full OMat24 size.

fits_no_version.finding: Table H.1: larger EquiformerV2 models (S 31M, M 87M, L 154M parameters) give slightly lower OMat24 test energy and force MAE, e.g. WBM test energy 15.96, 14.87, 14.57 meV/atom. No scaling fit is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For materials MLIPs trained on OMat24, larger EquiformerV2 models give modestly lower test errors.

record.problems: The relevant learning curves are shown in a figure without exact values or a reported power-law fit; they do not provide evidence about the claim's language-model measures.

untested.parts: All: no language-model held-out loss scaling.
All: no extrapolation of fitted laws.
Whether a power-law form holds for materials MLIPs: the learning curves are not fitted or tested for power-law form.
All: no exponent or fitting-choice analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the scaling-law reference appears only in the introduction as motivation. The paper offers no specific argument about any version. In Table H.1 as extracted, the eSEN-30M and eqV2-S rows have identical values, possibly a table-extraction or source duplication error. Model-size differences in Table H.1 are small, with no fit.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameter count, tokens, and compute.
Extrapolating language-model loss from smaller runs to much larger runs.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count on language-model loss.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the reported curve is not fitted or assessed as a power law.
Predictability of downstream language-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model exponents and compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices.
